components.text: Whether a transcendent uncaused creator explains the universe rather than merely relocating the origin question.
Whether uncertainty about cosmic origins supplies positive support for an intelligent creator.
The decisive demand is whether beginning and fine-tuning warrant an uncaused transcendent intelligence.
The creator's exemption from the demand for an origin requires a relevant asymmetry.
The fine-tuning evidence and its comparative likelihood under design require assessment.
Whether materialism makes human reasoning and belief generally untrustworthy.
Whether uncertainty before the Big Bang warrants asserting God.
Whether physical inquiry requires a supernatural explanatory foundation.
The decisive demand is whether uncertainty before the Big Bang licenses a confident supernatural conclusion.
The claim that physical regularities require divine explanation is challenged by scientific inquiry.
The specific argument that material cognition undermines rational trust requires an answer.
Whether biological information requires an intelligent source rather than natural developmental mechanisms.
Whether evolutionary history supplies a natural alternative to biological design.
The decisive demand is whether DNA's functional information requires an intelligent source.
The broader theological dependence on Eden and original sin is raised but does not answer the moral-standard inference.
Whether appeal to a transcendent cause merely substitutes God for an unresolved natural-origin gap.
Whether further natural inquiry could in principle identify the cause of the whole natural universe.
The decisive demand is whether a natural cause could explain the totality of nature.
The request to wait for further natural inquiry is challenged as category-inappropriate for nature's total cause.
Whether apparent order and low-probability life-supporting conditions establish intentional design.
Whether transcendence of a cosmic cause establishes purposive intelligence.
The decisive fine-tuning demand is whether observer-compatible conditions are better explained by design.
The separate claim that nature's total cause must transcend nature requires an answer.
Whether biological complexity is analogous to an instantaneous random arrangement requiring intelligence.
Whether cumulative retained increments over many generations provide the relevant natural mechanism.
The decisive demand is whether natural processes can cumulatively generate biological complexity and information.
The instantaneous random-spill analogy must accurately represent mutation, inheritance, and selection.
Whether morality without a divine standard reduces to irresponsible personal opinion.
Whether claimed divine objectivity can itself encourage harmful moral certainty.
The decisive demand is whether moral judgment requires an objective standard beyond human social life.
The practical consequences of claiming divine moral authority for human responsibility require comparison.
The metaethical claim that objective evil presupposes God requires a direct answer.
Whether objective evil supports God despite severe apparently undeserved suffering under divine control.
Whether infant cancer is compatible with omnipotence, omniscience, and complete benevolence.
The decisive demand is whether invoking objective good answers severe suffering under classical divine attributes.
The internal tension among omnipotence, omniscience, benevolence, and infant suffering requires explanation.
Whether divine foreknowledge itself causes created agents' choices and removes their freedom.
Whether free choice explains infant cancer and other non-agential suffering.
The freedom defense requires distinguishing divine foreknowledge from causal determination of human choices.
The claim that human agents remain responsible for their choices is supported by distinguishing knowledge from causation.
The specific existence of infant cancer under divine goodness and power requires explanation.
Whether freedom or foreknowledge distinctions explain why childhood leukemia is needed for any wider good.
Whether later or eternal goods justify severe suffering under an omnipotent God.
The decisive demand is whether divine power could achieve proposed goods without childhood leukemia.
The claim that evil may yield later or eternal good requires a necessity or means-end warrant.
The narrower distinction between knowledge and causal determination is not itself denied.
Whether human judgments of justice, honesty, freedom, and better conduct can have force without objective standards.
Whether atheistic social responsibility supplies an ontological ground rather than merely using evaluative language.
Whether criticism of divine action presupposes objective moral standards.
The decisive demand is whether human moral evaluation can have normative authority under atheism.
Appeals to proof and better reasoning allegedly require standards that theism can ground.
Judging childhood leukemia as a worse means allegedly invokes an objective evaluative standard.
Whether the biological design inference is testable rather than protected from natural counterevidence.
Whether natural processes could produce specified complex biological information.
The decisive demand is whether the biological design inference can be tested against natural production of specified information.
Established evolution is relevant only if natural mechanisms generate the specified complex information at issue.
Whether atheism can account for moral concern and cooperative conduct without a divine ground.
Whether natural social capacities explain use of evaluative standards rather than their objective authority.
The decisive demand is whether compassion and cooperative moral conduct require divine grounding.
The natural origin of empathy is offered against the claim that atheism supplies no evaluative capacities.
The separate normative question of objective moral authority beyond evolved preferences requires an answer.
Whether conceptual deduction of transcendence is sufficient without independent evidence for a law-transcending deity.
Whether cosmic premises specifically establish a timeless, spaceless intelligent being.
Whether theistic grounding claims require an independently supported divine basis.
The decisive demand is whether conceptual deduction alone establishes a law-transcending divine cause.
The move demands independent evidence for the timeless and spaceless divine attributes.
The biological design test and its claimed falsifier require separate empirical assessment.
